title: Learning saxophone from a soldier named Red
summary: Howard says a saxophonist called Red from the Army inspired him to take up the saxophone, which was unusual in Los Angeles then.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And so when you first came here, you probably--what--played mostly cornet, you played cornet, too?
Cornet, yeah.
Well, when did you start playing saxophone?
When did I start playing saxophone?
You were playing sax back in Ohio, right?
Yeah, I played saxophone back in Ohio.
So when you came out here, were you playing saxophone--
Nah.
as often, as you did--?
Not as often.
Saxophone must've been unusual, then?
It was unusual, quite unusual.
It was some new thing, at that period.
It was a new thing.
Yeah, a trump cornet? (chuckle)
Oh, yeah. I'n give you a little story that'll confirm what I'm saying. There was a fellow by the name Red--
Could you put the mike a little closer?

--fellow by the name of Red. He played the saxophone. And he was in the Army. And that's what got me onto a saxophone. I remember just as well, as it was just yesterday. I can see him standin' up here now; we called him Red. And he got a saxophone, and I got one, too. That's what made me start to playin' a saxophone. And I wish I could think of Red's name. He came here with the Army. Yeah, Red.
That was back in Ohio, wasn't it?
Yeah, uh-huh.
When was the first time you played saxophone professionally here in Los Angeles? First job-- you played sax?
When was it? Oh, I don't remember, dear. That's too hard. I can't remember it. But it was when--
How old were you?
How old was I?
That would help us on the date.
(inaudible)
Who were you playing with, when you first started playing saxophone here, professionally? First job you got on saxophone?
Don't remember who it was with?

Uh--I just picked up a saxophone, and went on, a'blowin' on it (chuckle) at that time. Forget it. I can't make it. You know, excuse me please, but do you know, you people have asked us so many things today that pin you down so fast that you can't remember it all, those things.
You can't remember it all, but you've given us so many answers today. It's just wonderful.
A great day. I think so.
